subtype: Approach: accepting a loss and learning from it [Revision]
passage: I'm Rafiq. We finished third at the inter-school quiz, and I felt small on the stage, holding a certificate I did not want. Mehak squeezed my hand, and I turned my face away. On the bus my chest still hurt. But I did not want to spend the whole ride feeling terrible, so afterwards I went back to the quiz master and asked, "Which questions did we miss?" The quiz master read out six. I copied them on the back of my ticket. At home I stuck the ticket to the wall. Next year, those six will be the first things I look up.

qa.q: Where did Rafiq write the six missed questions?
qa.a: Rafiq copied them on the back of a ticket.

qa.q: How did Rafiq feel on the stage and on the bus?
qa.a: Rafiq felt small and hurt, shown by turning the face away and the pain in the chest, but did not want to stay in it. 😢

qa.q: What alternative approach could Rafiq use next year, and why?
qa.a: Rafiq could hold mock rounds with Mehak and focus on the weak areas early. Practising together spots gaps long before the quiz day.

qa.q: How might Mehak have felt on the stage?
qa.a: Mehak squeezed Rafiq's hand, so Mehak probably felt sympathetic and wanted to comfort someone who was clearly upset.

grounding: After finishing third, a child feels upset but asks the quiz master which questions were missed, writes them down and plans to study those areas next year.

subtype: Approach: accepting a loss and learning from it [Revision]
passage:
Teacher's note, inter-school quiz, Saturday
Pranav's team finished third out of eight. When the results were read out, Pranav went very quiet and blinked hard, and I thought he might cry. On the bus I let him be. But before we left the hall, he walked up to the quiz master by himself and asked politely which questions his team had missed. The quiz master showed him the sheet. Pranav copied the missed questions into his notebook: two on rivers, one on space, one on a famous painting. On the bus he said, "Next year I'll know these." I have told Tanuja ma'am, who runs the quiz club, and she will help him make a study plan.
- Class teacher

qa.q: What position did Pranav's team finish in?
qa.a: Pranav's team finished third out of eight.

qa.q: How was Pranav feeling when the results were read out?
qa.a: He was upset and disappointed, going quiet and blinking hard as if close to tears.

qa.q: What else could Pranav do with the questions he copied?
qa.a: He could turn them into a list of topics to read about, one each week, so the study plan is steady and small.

qa.q: How does Pranav's question look to the quiz master?
qa.a: The quiz master sees a boy who wants to learn, not just win, and is willing to show him the sheet.

grounding: It shows a child who is upset after finishing third, then asking the quiz master which questions he missed and planning to study those areas.

subtype: Approach: accepting a loss and learning from it [Revision]
passage:
Saturday
Diary, we came third. THIRD. After all that practice. I wanted to kick the chair. Papa just put his hand on my shoulder and didn't say anything, which helped. Then I remembered what Aditi didi said once: the questions you miss tell you what to learn. So I went up to the quiz master while they were packing up, and asked, "Sir, can I see which ones we got wrong?" He looked surprised but showed me. I wrote them all down: three on the Constitution, two on birds, one on old coins. Papa said, "That's my boy." I'm still upset. But now I have a list for next year, and the Constitution ones are first.
- Kiran

qa.q: How many questions on the Constitution did Kiran write down?
qa.a: Kiran wrote down three on the Constitution.

qa.q: How did Kiran feel right after hearing they came third?
qa.a: Kiran felt angry and disappointed, wanting to kick the chair.

qa.q: What else could Kiran do to keep the list from being forgotten over the year?
qa.a: Kiran could pin the list inside the study cupboard and tick off each topic after reading about it.

qa.q: How does the quiz master see Kiran's request?
qa.a: The quiz master is surprised, maybe pleased, and willing to show which ones went wrong.

grounding: It shows a child upset at finishing third who asks the quiz master about missed questions, writes them down and plans to study them.
